title: Document markup example is invalid
author: dbstraight

comments.body:
I can understand why you might see it that way.

The directive you're referring to terminates with the curly brace, so `"curious"` is a new subdirective. Here's how Confetti would parse the entire document:

Note that I've enclosed arguments with angle brackets and denoted subdirectives with square brackets and indention.

```
<chapter> <The Raven>
<author> <Edgar Allan Poe>
<section> <First Act> [
    <paragraph> [
        <Once upon a midnight dreary, while I pondered, weak and weary,>
        <Over many a quaint and > <bold> [
            <curious>
        ]
        < volume of forgotten lore->
    ]
    <paragraph> [
        <While I nodded, nearly napping, suddenly there came a tapping,>
        <As of some one > <italic> [
            <gently>
        ]
        < rapping-rapping at my chamber door.>
    ]
]
```

An application would need to recognize that when the last argument is "bold" or "italic" that there (1) must be subdirectives and (2) those subdirectives are to be visually styled as **bold** or _italic_.
